blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is an independent constitutional authority established under Article 324.
The Commission currently comprises the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and two Election Commissioners, all enjoying equal decision-making powers.
Commissioners hold office for a term of 6 years or until reaching 65 years of age, whichever comes earlier.
The CEC enjoys security of tenure and can only be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge.
ECI's authority covers administrative, quasi-judicial, and advisory functions, including binding advice on disqualification of MPs and MLAs.

blocks.content: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is one of the most important constitutional bodies in India.
It is responsible for conducting free, fair, impartial and transparent elections in the country.
The success of Indian democracy largely depends upon the independent functioning of the Election Commission.
It ensures that political power is transferred peacefully and democratically.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar regarded free and fair elections as the backbone of democracy.
The Election Commission is established under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution. Article 324 provides:

items:
• Superintendence of elections
  • Direction and control of elections
  • Conduct of elections to:
    • Parliament
    • State Legislatures
    • Office of President
    • Office of Vice-President

Conduct of elections to:

blocks.content: Thus, ECI is a constitutional authority, not a statutory body.
Originally, the Election Commission was a single-member body. In 1989, it became a multi-member body.
All three have equal powers and take decisions by majority.

ECI is a Constitutional Body under Article 324, not a statutory body.
ECI conducts elections for Parliament, State Legislatures, President, and Vice-President, but NOT local body/panchayat elections.
Removal procedure differs: CEC can only be removed like a Supreme Court Judge, whereas Election Commissioners are removed by the President on the recommendation of the CEC.
ECI's advice to the President or Governor regarding disqualification of MPs and MLAs is legally binding.

blocks.content: The Election Commission of India is the guardian of democracy.
Its independence, integrity and efficiency determine the quality of elections in India. A strong Election Commission ensures a strong democracy.
